newsitem.title: GERMANY: Key week ahead for record-chasing German shares.
newsitem.headline: Key week ahead for record-chasing German shares.

text.p: Next week could be make-or-break time for the German share market, dealers said on Friday, at the end of a week which saw stocks advance more than two percent despite widespread expectations for a correction.

Not only are key German economic data expected -- including the influential IFO index -- but the dollar is likely to be a strong guide and a triple-witching option expiry next Friday could strongly influence cash market prices.
"We've had 13 days of unbroken gains," noted one trader. "Everyone is waiting for the correction and it will have to come -- the big mystery is the timing."

Buoyed by positive U.S.economic data, the IBIS DAX index was up two points at 3,258.86 points at 1426 GMT, some 14 points below its intraday high, but still ten points above the DAX index bourse closing level -- up 18.870 points at 3,248.18 points.
The U.S. reports revealed, among other data, that January producer prices fell 0.3 percent.
"The basic message is -- moderate growth and low inflation. It couldn't be better," said one Munich dealer.
At the same time, a slight weakening in the dollar from its intraday highs of around 1.69 marks was weighing on prices.
And despite an overall strong climate, there was a widespread feeling that the market needs breathing space -- with some dealers predicting a drop of at least 50 DAX points in the near future.
On the upside, dealers said the next target level for the DAX -- which has already advanced some 14 percent this year --was pegged at between 3,300 and 3,350 points.

Dealers disagreed on whether more liquidity could come into the market at these heady levels, although most noted that investor activity had been markedly low on Friday, when most gains were attributed to short-covering.
The approach of Friday's triple witching was expected to impact prices strongly next week.
"I think it's key," said one dealer who specialises in technicals. "And at the moment it looks as though the expiry will have a supporting effect."
On individual sectors, banks were expected to continue to take centre stage, although they are seen as at some risk of profit taking after strong gains in the past week.
On Friday afternoon, Deutsche Bank led volumes and outperformed the broader market with gains of 38 pfennigs to 86.69 marks.

Meanwhile Metallgesellschaft AG was up 97 pfennigs at 34.22 marks as it continued to benefit from relief at its apparent decision on Thursday evening not to buy into industrial group Agiv -- a move some investors feared would have harmed its earnings.
Utility Viag AG remained under pressure after posting earnings in line with expectations, which dealers said took a lot of speculative interest from the stock.
Viag was down 8.50 marks at 707 marks in afternoon trade.
